chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Huzayfa ibn Mansur, who said:

I accompanied Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and he was heading towards Makkah. So when he prayed, he said: 'O Allah, free our way, and improve our travel, and improve our health.' And every time he ascended a hillock, he said: 'O Allah, for You is the Nobility over every nobility.'

key_terms.خَلِّ سَبِيلَنَا: Free our way / Ease our path

ai.seo_question: What are the specific supplications recited by the Imams during travel and when ascending hills?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi*, this hadith highlights the Imam’s practice of invoking divine facilitation and well-being while traveling, reflecting the Shia emphasis on integrating spiritual remembrance with daily activities. The specific dhikr upon ascending a height acknowledges Allah’s absolute honor, a concept deeply rooted in the Quranic description of the heavens and the divine throne.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Huzeyfa Bin Mansour who said,

‘I accompanied Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and he<sup>asws</sup> was heading towards Makkah. So when he<sup>asws</sup> Prayed, he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Free our way, and better our<sup>asws</sup> travelling, and better our health’. And, every time he<sup>asws</sup> ascended a hillock, said: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! For You<sup>azwj</sup> is the Nobility over every nobility’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Hudhayfah ibn Mansur who has said the following: “I accompanied abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, on the way to Makkah and when he completed his salat (prayer) he said, ‘O Allah, open the way for us. Make our journey and our health full of goodness.’ Whenever he climbed a higher place, he would say, ‘You possess highness and You are over all goodness.’”
